title: Crashproof reservation heuristics and de-escalation playbook for noisy tenants
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Summary: A production capacity event on 2026-03-06 exposed a cascade where a tenant-level KV cache growth bug combined with an aggressive burst policy and a reservations mis-sizing heuristic caused sustained eviction storms and high tail latency for multiple Dedicated clusters. This ticket captures proposed long-term mitigations, playbook updates, and measurable rollout criteria so we don't regress on noisy-tenant containment or reservation correctness.
root_cause: Telemetry regression during a recent allocator refactor (allocator v2) caused per-tenant `active_connection` samples to be undercounted. The reservation right-sizing job used that metric to scale down soft reservations; several tenants were reduced below observed working-set needs. One affected tenant concurrently had a memory leak in its KV caching layer that allowed its prefix cache to grow without eviction under burst. The existing burst token-bucket allowed short bursts to exceed soft reservations when GPUs reported additional headroom, which produced neighbor noise and triggered eviction cascades.
mitigation_taken: Emergency rollback of allocator v2 reservation shrink heuristic (rolled back 2026-03-06 21:10 UTC)
Temporary hard cap placed on burst window to 25% above soft reservation for P0 tenants (applied 2026-03-06 22:05 UTC)
Applied emergency per-tenant KV cache eviction policy for affected clusters (eviction priority heuristic tightened, 2026-03-07 02:30 UTC)
Rebalanced reservations to previous steady-state baselines for impacted tenants (coord with SRE and account owners)
Enabled synthetic tail-latency monitors and increased telemetry retention for last-12h allocator logs
action_items: A1: Implement reservation tapering: change resize job to require 24h of trend below threshold before shrinking reservation (owner: Liam Chen, est: 3) due: 2026-03-30
A2: Burst circuit-breaker: introduce per-tenant burst-circuit that transitions to 'restricted' state after sustained eviction rate > 0.5% over 5m (owner: Marisol Ortega, est: 5) due: 2026-04-02
A3: KV cache per-tenant cap and telemetry: add soft and hard caps to KV cache plus per-tenant cache-size telemetry and eviction counters (owner: Omar Greenwood, est: 3) due: 2026-03-28
A4: Fix allocator telemetry regression: add end-to-end test and alert on undercounting `active_connection` samples (owner: Priya Nair, est: 2) due: 2026-03-20
A5: Reservation sanity-checks in rollout: require canary that verifies per-tenant observed memory/headroom is within 10% of expected before applying shrink (owner: Liam Chen, est: 2) due: 2026-03-26
A6: Playbook update: document incident response flows (isolation, reassigning soft reservations, emergency rollback) and train on-call (owner: SRE Team, est: 1) due: 2026-03-18
A7: Load tests & chaos: add synthetic noisy-tenant tests to nightly suite and run eviction-storm stress tests against Dedicated clusters (owner: Testing infra, est: 4) due: 2026-04-06

A8: Dashboards & Alerts: create dashboard tile for per-tenant eviction-rate, KV cache growth rate, and reservation shrink events; add PagerDuty escalation on sustained eviction spikes (owner: Console Observability, est: 2) due: 2026-03-22
acceptance_criteria: Reservation tapering is active in staging and verified with synthetic workloads (shrink only after 24h signal)
Burst circuit-breaker opens and forces burst limit reduction during noisy-tenant simulation without impacting other tenants' baseline throughput
KV cache per-tenant caps enforced in staging and noted in telemetry, with no memory regressions in 72h soak
Allocator telemetry regression test merged and present in CI with a blocking alert if undercount occurs
Runbook updated and two SRE engineers have exercised the playbook in a drill
risks_and_tradeoffs: Tapering delays shrink actions and could increase steady-state allocated GPU minutes (cost up) until the 24h window completes
Circuit-breaker aggressiveness may throttle legitimate bursty workloads; we will provide tenant-level opt-in higher-burst contracts (Dedicated burst-tier) for managed customers
Hard caps on KV cache risk increased eviction rates for some models that rely on large prefixes; caps must be tunable per-tenant and surfaced in console
test_plan: Create a suite of noisy-tenant scenarios: high short-lived spike (1s-1m), sustained ramp (10m-2h), KV cache leak emulation
Inject spike during reservation shrink window to validate tapering prevents under-allocation
Simulate multi-tenant eviction cascades in shared-Pool staging to validate circuit-breaker isolation
Metric regression checks: ensure no increase in 99th latency for baseline tenants over 72h after rollout
